q: What is a strong option set for solution analysis?
options: Several materially different options, including do-nothing or minimal change
One requested solution with no baseline
A list of vendor names only
A technical design chosen before discovery
why: Credible alternatives enable meaningful comparison and reveal whether change is needed.

q: When should comparison criteria be agreed?
options: After seeing which option scores highest
why: Pre-agreed criteria reduce biased evaluation.

q: What should accompany a weighted score?
options: Evidence, assumptions and uncertainty for each rating
A claim that the total is objective
why: Scoring can organize discussion but does not make subjective inputs factual.

q: What should a BA provide to an architect?
options: Business outcomes, process context, volumes, constraints and risk tolerance
A mandated database design without rationale
why: Architecture partners need the business context and measurable constraints to shape options.

q: Which is an appropriate business requirement?
options: 95% of matching runs finish within the agreed time for target volume
Write code in a preferred language
why: Business-facing quality needs should be measurable without prescribing design unnecessarily.

q: Who owns technical architecture decisions?
options: The designated architecture and engineering owners
why: The BA informs technical design but does not automatically own it.

q: How should a vague quality need like “fast” be improved?
options: Define scenario, threshold, measurement method and owner
Replace it with a feature name
why: A measurable quality attribute can be verified.

q: Why should control needs be treated as solution behavior?
options: Controls affect requirements, workflow, evidence and exception handling
why: Controls need to be designed and verified as part of the solution.

q: Who should validate a control threshold?
why: Control owners confirm acceptable risk and evidence requirements.

q: What should a data-flow analysis include?
options: Source, owner, meaning, timing, quality rules and consumers
why: Data lineage and ownership matter across systems and decisions.

q: Which is an important integration failure condition?
options: A feed arrives late or contains duplicate records
why: Late or duplicate inputs can affect matching and controls.

q: Why distinguish local configuration from shared definitions?
options: It allows needed variation without creating inconsistent meaning
It means data quality is irrelevant
why: Shared semantics can coexist with approved local settings.

q: What is a useful business-rule table field?
options: Condition and outcome with owner, effective date and exception path
why: Rule tables should make behavior and governance testable.

q: Why separate policy from implementation logic?
options: Business owners approve policy while technical teams implement behavior
It gives the BA all authority
why: Clear ownership prevents confusing policy choices with technical realization.

q: What is a safe rule for automated matching?
options: Do not let a match rule authorize write-off without approved control design
Every match should write off automatically
why: Automated matching and financial write-off are different actions with different risks.

q: What should cross-team traceability connect?
options: Outcome, requirement, delivery item, test evidence and owner
why: Traceability supports impact analysis across teams and controls.

q: A requested change affects migration and training. What should be assessed?
options: End-to-end impacts, trade-offs and what work is displaced
Nothing if the change is agile
why: Scope changes can affect several workstreams beyond the visible feature.

q: What should be done with deferred scope?
options: Record what is deferred, why and which outcome or risk it affects
why: Clear deferral records support future prioritization.

q: Why involve technical partners early?
options: They can expose feasibility, integration and migration constraints before commitments
why: Early collaboration helps shape feasible options and dependencies.

q: What is a good acceptance target for a high-value write-off control?
options: Every override records authorized user, reason, approval and timestamp
The feature has a green status
why: A control need should define observable evidence and authorization.
